news.title: Fouzi Lekjaa and the ‘World Cup 2030 Government’: From Pitch to Premiership
news.lede: This past July 25, Fouzi Lekjaa — Morocco's Minister Delegate for the Budget and, since 2014, president of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (RMFF) — formally joined the Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM) , taking an immediate seat on its Political Bureau . PAM's national coordinator Fatima-Zahra El Mansouri announced the news during the party's National Council in Salé, ending weeks of speculation and instantly becoming one of the most consequential political stories of Morocco's pre-electoral season. It arrived seven weeks before the legislative elections of 23 September 2026, which PAM has openly declared its ambition to finish first. Le Monde captured the moment by describing Lekjaa as "putting on the suit of a prime-ministerial contender," and Moroccan outlets have floated the idea, however speculative, of a future "World Cup 2030 government" led by the FRMF chief.

news.title: Portugal rejects calls to drop Morocco from 2030 World Cup co-hosting
news.lede: Portugal has reaffirmed its commitment to co-hosting the 2030 FIFA World Cup with Morocco and Spain, rejecting calls from the opposition Livre party to remove Morocco from the joint hosting arrangement following the recent migration crisis in Ceuta. Portugal’s Minister of Culture, Youth and Sport, Margarida Balseiro Lopes, said the government remained committed to delivering what she described as “the best World Cup ever,” according to public broadcaster RTP. “We want it to be a tournament of the highest standard, both in sporting and competitive terms, but we also want it to be an opportunity to bring people and cultures together,” Lopes said. She added that preparations for the tournament had been underway across several government ministries, not only those responsible for sports.

news.title: Football vs Wall Street: Inside the fight for the World Cup's soul
news.lede: LONDON, Aug 9 — What does artificial intelligence (AI) have to do with the World Cup? Quite a lot, according to the tech investors who were prepared to put billions of dollars into Fifa's proposed private investment vehicle before fierce opposition forced the governing body to shelve the plan. The thinking behind the proposal was simple, according to a BBC article published yesterday. As AI transforms entertainment and increasingly replaces human work in areas such as film and music, some experiences may become more valuable precisely because they cannot be replicated by technology — and football is one of them.

news.title: Sexual favor scandal revives doubts over Korea's historic 2002 World Cup semifinal run
news.lede: Police officers leave the Korea Football Association (KFA) headquarters in Seoul, Friday, after searching the office to investigate whether KFA executives unlawfully intervened in the hiring process of former national team head coach Hong Myung-bo. Yonhap The disclosure of the national football association’s alleged provision of sexual entertainment to foreign referees between 2011 and 2012 is expanding beyond national disgrace toward doubts over the legitimacy of Korea’s landmark 2002 World Cup semifinal advancement. It has revived the 24-year-old suspicions that the Korean national team had been favored during the World Cup matches and thus gained the exceptional result, although there were no grounds to back the suspicion of any illegality involved.

news.title: [ED] Korean football needs reckoning, not another apology
news.lede: The area around Korea Football Park in Cheonan, South Chungcheong Province, was quiet Thursday as police conducted a search and seizure of the Korea Football Association. Police began the operation at about 9 a.m., sending all employees outside. Yonhap The Korea Football Association (KFA) has apologized. Following Korea’s disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign, a parliamentary hearing, a police search of KFA headquarters and renewed scrutiny of long-buried allegations, the KFA has acknowledged that public trust in the institution has been badly damaged.

news.title: Infantino admits World Cup sell-off ‘errors’ but wins full backing to stay FIFA president
news.lede: Rabat (IANS): Gianni Infantino admitted mistakes were made in the process of trying to sell off the World Cup to private investment and apologised for "errors" he made, but the senior executives "reaffirmed their full support" for him to remain FIFA president after a crisis meeting in Morocco. . Infantino was forced to withdraw his plan to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA's tournaments, after it triggered widespread opposition from UEFA, Concacaf, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and several national associations, as well as criticism from within FIFA.. Secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, who was at Wednesday's meeting, wrote in an internal memo sent to Fifa staff on Tuesday that the situation is "a sad and reproachable series of events"..

news.title: Tragedy Beyond Football: Lionel Messi's Father Passes Away, Causing Him to Cry at the World Cup
news.lede: The health problems of Jorge Messi became known during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. In June, the family reported that he was undergoing treatment and was under medical supervision. At that time, relatives noted that his condition was improving and requested respect for the family's right to privacy. It was during that period that Lionel Messi could not hold back tears after the Argentina national team's match against Algeria.

news.title: Morocco, Algeria reach WAFCON semifinals and qualify for FIFA World Cup
news.lede: The North African nations become the first teams from the continent to qualify for next year's World Cup in Brazil.
